description_paragraphs: Public inputs include dimension $d$ and $D_K$, $\beta$, $\varepsilon$, and $\sigma$, together with the stated initial-point and feasible-domain information. Analytic representations of hidden functions, operators, or matrices are not revealed.

$$
z\in K\longmapsto G_F(z;\xi)
$$
Exact Euclidean projection onto the known set is allowed. Its calls are recorded separately and excluded from the primary query count.

Let $\mathcal H_t$ denote the full history before query t. Conditional on $\mathcal H_t,z_t$, the response $G_t\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfies $\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal H_t,z_t]=F(z_t)$ and $\mathbb E[\|G_t-F(z_t)\|_2^2\mid\mathcal H_t,z_t]\le\sigma^2$. Each call uses an independent fresh sample.

No reusable sample identifier or cross-point sample reuse is available. No mean-square smoothness of sample gradients or operators is additionally assumed. Blocks within a full vector may be correlated.

bounds.derivation: On $K=[-D_K/2,D_K/2]$, take constant operators $F_\pm=\pm a$ with $a=8\varepsilon/D_K$. Each response is an independent Gaussian observation with mean $\pm a$ and variance $\sigma^2$, independent of the query point. An output on the wrong half-axis has gap at least $aD_K/2=4\varepsilon$. Expected gap at most $\varepsilon$ therefore implies testing error at most $1/4$. The per-sample KL divergence is $2a^2/\sigma^2$, and two-point testing yields $N\ge c\sigma^2/a^2$. Constant operators are monotone and have Lipschitz constant zero, so they belong to the declared class.
bounds.lower_scope_type_note: Two-point testing, zero-query indistinguishability, and nonexistence counterexamples cover arbitrary privately randomized policies. These are not linear-span lower bounds.
